text:
- chief complaint: Sharp right-sided abdominal/flank pain below the ribs for several days, previously diagnosed as a kidney stone on CT.
- history of present illness: Pain radiates to the lower abdomen and groin, intermittently severe, with burning on urination and occasional dark-appearing urine (no frank blood). Acetaminophen has not helped. Patient reports nausea without vomiting. Prior kidney stones passed, but this episode is taking longer. Father has a history of kidney stones.
- physical examination: No abdominal tenderness, rebound, guarding, or peritoneal signs. Positive right costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness. CT shows a 0.5 cm right proximal ureteral stone without hydronephrosis.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: Right flank pain radiating to groin, dysuria, dark urine, nausea.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: Oxycodone 5 mg every 6–8 hours as needed for pain, alternating with acetaminophen.
- follow-up instructions: Increase fluid intake, strain urine, basic metabolic panel, urinalysis, and urine culture ordered. Return in 1–2 weeks; contact the doctor for worsening symptoms. Lithotripsy or ureteroscopy discussed if symptoms persist.
